correctness.rationale: A non-psh C^2 weight has a strictly negative Levi trace against some positive definite Hermitian P. The source identifies every such P with an affine coordinate matrix. Strict negativity persists under small changes of center and matrix; the nonzero set of the fixed holomorphic f is dense, and Gaussian-rational centers and invertible matrices are dense. For the selected rational affine test, change of variables gives exactly the source tuple (w_1,...,w_n,M). Proposition 3.8 yields tr(i∂∂bar φ) >= -n^2/M^2 by an epsilon→infinity limit; taking only integer epsilon is sufficient, and then integer M→infinity gives the contradiction. On pseudoconvex domains the converse is the classical Skoda theorem.

value.rationale: The source's hypothesis ranges over an infinite-dimensional class of holomorphic tuples and continuous parameter families. The accepted result replaces it by one explicit countable family while retaining equivalence on bounded pseudoconvex domains. This gives a structurally separable positivity criterion and identifies exactly which freedoms in the converse proof are dispensable; it is more than a routine numerical sharpening.
